# Breaking Down the United Healthcare Disaster: What’s REALLY Going On? | Real Eisman Playbook Ep. 26

First listed: 2025-09-22 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Breaking Down the United Healthcare Disaster: What’s REALLY Going On? | Real Eisman Playbook Ep. 26](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L6QSH_ZmYxI) - 2025-09-22
- [Substack: Breaking Down the United Healthcare Disaster: What’s REALLY Going On? | Real Eisman Playbook Ep. 26](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/breaking-down-the-united-healthcare-fa5) - 2025-09-22

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Michael Ha explains why UnitedHealth difficulties extend beyond insurance pricing to Optum Health, risk-adjustment changes and the quality of reported earnings. Eisman presses for a plain-language model, adopts concern about coding exposure and criticizes limited granular disclosure.

The episode identifies real Optum pressure and a disclosed V28 funding headwind. Guest forecasts of a prolonged decline must be separated from Eisman disclosure-based caution. Several causal allegations remain unproved, and the discussion confuses the MLR ceiling on nonmedical spending with a guaranteed profit margin. Subsequent results show partial recovery, not proof that every structural issue has disappeared.

<a id="youtube-L6QSH_ZmYxI-c016"></a>
### 016. Health insurance has a universal government-mandated maximum gross margin of 15%.

**Wrong** | Michael Ha | explanation | major

[Source at 14:11-14:39](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L6QSH_ZmYxI&t=851s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The applicable MLR can be 80% or 85%, and it measures clinical and quality spending with regulatory adjustments. The 15% framing is not universal.

Assessment test: Apply the correct market-specific MLR calculation.

- [Medical loss ratio requirements](https://www.cms.gov/marketplace/private-health-insurance/medical-loss-ratio) (2026-03-13): Applicable minimum ratios are 80% or 85%. The remaining amount pays administration as well as profit; an MLR threshold does not guarantee a net profit margin.
- [Medicare Advantage medical loss ratio](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/health-drug-plans/medical-loss-ratio) (2026-11-10): Medicare Advantage has an 85% minimum MLR and reporting/remittance requirements; the complement is not guaranteed profit.

<a id="youtube-L6QSH_ZmYxI-c017"></a>
### 017. Delegating 85% of premiums to providers lets an insurer lock in its maximum 15% profit.

**Wrong** | Michael Ha | explanation | major

[Source at 14:39-15:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L6QSH_ZmYxI&t=879s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The retained amount must also fund administration and other expenses. A contractual delegation does not guarantee net profit or remove all risk.

Assessment test: Bridge premium to medical cost, administration, taxes and net income.

- [Medicare Advantage medical loss ratio](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/health-drug-plans/medical-loss-ratio) (2026-11-10): Medicare Advantage has an 85% minimum MLR and reporting/remittance requirements; the complement is not guaranteed profit.

<a id="youtube-L6QSH_ZmYxI-c018"></a>

Vertical integration can capture provider economics, but Eisman repeats the premise that 15% is insurer profit. MLR limits nonmedical spending; administrative costs and consolidating eliminations still matter.

- [Medicare Advantage medical loss ratio](https://www.cms.gov/medicare/health-drug-plans/medical-loss-ratio) (2026-11-10): Medicare Advantage has an 85% minimum MLR and reporting/remittance requirements; the complement is not guaranteed profit.

<a id="youtube-L6QSH_ZmYxI-c048"></a>
### 048. Gains from selling businesses should not be treated as recurring operating performance.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 38:09-38:42](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L6QSH_ZmYxI&t=2289s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

A disposal gain is not income from the ongoing customer activity. Its legal GAAP classification can differ, so the analytical need is a clear recurring-earnings reconciliation.

Conditional reasoning: Selling an existing business realizes an asset value once; absent repeated asset depletion, the gain cannot be extrapolated as recurring income from the same operating base.

Assessment test: Identify gains and normalize the recurring earnings base.

Conditional reasoning: Disclosed in a filing and never disclosed are mutually inconsistent. Disclosure can still be insufficiently clear or detailed.

Assessment test: Inspect the precise filing language and earnings presentation.

Consolidated operating earnings rose to $6.6 billion from $4.3 billion. Guidance was raised to at least $20.50 adjusted EPS. Segment realignment and adjustments require care; recovery does not establish full restoration of the earlier franchise.

## Framework and tools

- Separate the insurance business from care delivery and pharmacy services.
- Distinguish repricing a short-duration contract from repairing a structurally impaired business.
- Question recurring earnings supported by asset sales.
- Require enough segment disclosure to test the investment thesis.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Segment operating profit and margin
- Medical loss ratio
- Risk-adjustment scores and HCC coding
- Before/after acquisition comparisons
- Value-based-care cohort margins
- Asset-sale gains and intercompany charges
- Scenario EPS and valuation multiples

## Source cautions

Michael Ha supplies the sell-side research and forecasts. Steve Eisman asks questions, sometimes explicitly adopts a premise, and gives his own disclosure-based investment view. These roles remain separate.
- Automatic captions repeatedly misspell Optum, Baird and corporate names. Original review prose corrects them.
- Opening montage repeats later discussion and is not counted twice.
- Allegations about coding, internal charges and sale arrangements are preserved as hypotheses or reports, not established fraud.
- 2026 segment realignment changes comparability of Optum figures.
